facts.statement: The only known specimen of Pegomastax was discovered during a 1966–1967 expedition in South Africa but was not formally described until 2012 by Paul Sereno.
facts.quote: The only known specimen was discovered in a 1966–1967 expedition in Transkei District of Cape Province, but was not described until 2012 when Paul Sereno named it as the new taxon Pegomastax africana.

facts.statement: The genus name Pegomastax means "strong jaw" in Greek, while the species name refers to its African origin.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from the Greek for "strong jaw", and the species name describes the provenance of Africa

facts.statement: The only known material of Pegomastax consists of a partial skull with a well-preserved lower jaw and teeth.
facts.quote: The only known material of Pegomastax included a partial skull with well-preserved lower jaw and teeth

facts.statement: Wear patterns on its teeth suggest Pegomastax was herbivorous, likely eating tougher plants than its relatives that lacked a canine tooth.
facts.quote: wear on the teeth suggests that Pegomastax had a herbivorous diet, possibly of tougher plant matter than relatives that lacked the canine

facts.statement: Pegomastax lived during the earliest Jurassic, specifically the Hettangian and Sinemurian epochs, approximately 200 to 190 million years ago.
facts.quote: This part of the formation is considered to be from the earliest Jurassic, the Hettangian and Sinemurian epochs from around 200 to 190 million years ago.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Pegomastax, accession number SAM-PK-K10488, was found at the Voyizane (or Voisana) locality in the Transkei District.
facts.quote: The specimen, given the accession number SAM-PK-K10488 was found alongside other heterodontosaurid material in Voisana

facts.statement: Pegomastax had a skull length of 73 mm, which is smaller than Heterodontosaurus (115 mm) but larger than Tianyulong (65 mm).
facts.quote: Pegomastax is estimated to have a skull length of 73 mm, compared to Heterodontosaurus at 115 mm and Tianyulong at 65 mm.

facts.statement: Unlike its relatives Heterodontosaurus, Abrictosaurus, and Lycorhinus, Pegomastax possessed a straight caniniform tooth at the front of its jaw.
facts.quote: A large caniniform tooth is present at the front of the jaw as in most other heterodontosaurids, but unlike in Heterodontosaurus, Abrictosaurus and Lycorhinus the caniniform is straight.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis recovered Pegomastax as a derived heterodontosaurid in the subfamily Heterodontosaurinae, with the South American taxon Manidens identified as its closest relative.
facts.quote: Pegomastax was recovered as a derived heterodontosaurid in the subfamily Heterodontosaurinae, united with all other African members of the family and the South American Manidens, which was identified as its closest relative

facts.statement: Some 2017 phylogenetic analyses alternatively resolve Pegomastax as the sister taxon to a group containing Heterodontosaurus and Lycorhinus.
facts.quote: Alternatively, Pegomastax has been resolved as the sister taxon of a group of Heterodontosaurus and Lycorhinus in the 2017 phylogenetic analysis of Daniel Madzia and colleagues

facts.statement: Researchers have noted that the internal relationships within Heterodontosauridae are weakly supported and require further investigation.
facts.quote: Han et al. noted that the internal relationships of Heterodontosauridae were weakly supported and needed more work.

facts.statement: Pegomastax was a parrot-like herbivore that measured no more than 60 centimeters from head to tail.
facts.quote: Desde la cabeza hasta la cola, el herbívoro parecido a un loro no medía más de 60 centímetros.

facts.statement: Pegomastax had a robust lower jaw with a short beak.
facts.quote: La mandíbula inferior era robusta, con un pico corto.

facts.statement: Like most other heterodontosaurids, Pegomastax possessed an enlarged canine-like tooth at the beginning of its lower jaw row, which may have served a defensive function.
facts.quote: Como la mayoría de los otros heterodontosáuridos, Pegomastax tenía un diente similar a un canino agrandado al comienzo de la fila de dientes de la mandíbula inferior, que puede haber tenido una función defensiva.

facts.statement: Although found during an expedition in 1966–1967, Pegomastax was not named until 2012.
facts.quote: Aunque encontrado en una expedición de 1966–1967, no se ha nombrado hasta 2012.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, SAM-PK-K10488, is a partial skull including a postorbital bone, both jaw bones, and a predentary.
facts.quote: El holotipo, SAM-PK-K10488, es un cráneo parcial que incluye un hueso postorbital, ambos huesos de la mandíbula y un predentario.

facts.statement: Pegomastax lived during the early Jurassic, approximately 200 to 190 million years ago (Hettangian to Sinemurian stages), in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 200 y 190 millones de años, entre el Hettangiense y el Sinemuriense, en lo que hoy es África.

facts.statement: The fossil was found in Voyizane, Joe Gqabi District Municipality, in the Western Cape province, within rocks from the upper Elliot Formation dating to the early Jurassic.
facts.quote: Se encontró en Voyizane, Joe Gqabi District Municipality, provincia del Cabo, en rocas de la parte superior de la Formación Elliot, que data de principios del Jurásico.

facts.statement: The genus Pegomastax was named by Sereno in 2012.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Sereno, 2012

facts.statement: The species Pegomastax africana was named by Sereno in 2012.
facts.quote: species_authority: Sereno, 2012

facts.statement: Pegomastax was recovered as a derived heterodontosaurid in the subfamily Heterodontosaurinae, closely related to the South American genus Manidens based on the asymmetrical shape and curvature of their dental crowns.
facts.quote: Pegomastax fue recuperado como un heterodontosáurido derivado en la subfamilia Heterodontosaurinae, unido a todos los demás miembros africanos de la familia y a Manidens de Sudamérica, que fue identificado como su pariente más cercano basándose en la forma asimétrica y la curvatura de sus coronas dentales.

facts.statement: There is debate regarding the function of heterodontosaurid canines, with suggestions ranging from omnivory and defense to processing tough, fibrous vegetation.
facts.quote: Barrett suggested in 2000 that the premaxillary teeth and dentary canine were indications of heterodontosaurids being omnivorous, while Butler and colleagues suggested in 2008 that they were likely used for defense and occasional omnivory, and Porro and colleagues suggested in 2011 that the caniniforms were an indication of a diet of more tough, fibrous vegetation.

facts.statement: Norman et al. (2011) suggested that heterodontosaurid canines were unlikely used for display or vegetation processing due to a lack of wear and evidence for sexual variation.
facts.quote: Norman et al. suggested in 2011 alternatively that the canines were unlikely to have been used for display or cropping and rooting vegetation, as there was no wear from use present and no strong evidence for sexual variation.

facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Sinemurian (201.4 to 192.9 million years ago)
